title: Breakfast Bake
steps: Cube bread and layer over the bottom of greased 9 x 12 in baking pan.
Brown sausage and drain. Pour over cubed bread and add a layer of shredded cheese.
In a separate bowl, mix together eggs, milk, ground mustard, and salt.
Pour mixture over the top of bread & cheese, cover and let sit overnight in refrigerator.
When ready to bake, place foil over the top and bake at 350°F for 50 to 60 minutes. Let sit 15 minutes prior to serving.

title: Banana Bread
fact: Growing up we had one cookbook “Betty Crocker”. Banana Bread was one of my favorite recipes I made throughout my lifetime.
ingredients: ½ cups unsalted butter, melted and cool
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Set oven rack to low position so tops of pans will be in center of oven. Grease bottoms only of 2 loaf pans 8½″ × 4½″ × 2½″ or 1 loaf pan, 9×5×3 inches.
In a large bowl mix together butter and sugar until light and creamy. Add eggs and blend.
Mash bananas with a fork in a separate bowl and blend into egg mixture. Add buttermilk and vanilla and mix well.
Fold in the dry ingredients until everything is mixed together.
Pour into prepared pan and bake 50 minutes; 9-inch loaf 1 hour. Test with toothpick — it should come out clean.
Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan. Place on wire rack, top side up, and cool completely, about 2 hours before slicing.
Wrap tightly and store at room temperature up to 4 days or refrigerate up to 10 days.
notes: Variations — add during mixing: Raisin Cinnamon Bread: 1½ cup raisins & 2 teaspoons cinnamon. Banana Nut Bread: 1 cup pecans or walnuts.

title: French Toast
fact: French toast was my favorite breakfast growing up in Beaumont. I made this recipe often for my children and now for my grandson Vincent. He loves his Nana’s French toast for breakfast.
ingredients: 4 slices white or wheat bread, cut in half
Canola or vegetable oil for frying
steps: Choose your bread and cut in half; set aside.
Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat.
In a medium bowl, whisk together egg yolks, milk, sugar, vanilla extract and cinnamon. Pour into a shallow dish.
Place slices of bread in egg mixture and let sit 10 to 20 seconds; flip and repeat for the other side.
Place the French toast in the skillet and cook about 3 minutes on each side. Remove and place on paper towel to absorb excess oil.
Serve with your favorite maple syrup, and sprinkle with powdered sugar.

title: Biscuit Donuts
fact: Growing up in the late 50’s early 60’s my sisters & I would make these donuts. I occasionally made these for my children who also enjoyed them.
steps: Heat oil in skillet on medium heat.
Separate biscuits, then with a small round cookie cutter, cut a hole in the center of each biscuit.
Place donuts into oil and fry on both sides until golden brown.
Drain on paper towel, let cool a bit, and coat both sides with powdered sugar.

title: 10 Can Soup
fact: A favorite go-to hearty soup for cold weather days, complements of my sister Denise. My family loves this soup.
ingredients: 2 cans Ranch Style Beans with jalapeño peppers
steps: In a skillet brown ground beef and drain grease.
In a 2½ to 3-quart pot, add all cans of vegetables and browned ground beef together and cook on medium for 30 minutes.

title: Chicken Vegetable Soup
fact: Enjoyed this soup at Emiel & Lena’s house in the late 1960’s. Lena made this soup at least once a month and usually added butter beans.
steps: Add water to a 10-quart pot and bring to a boil. Add chicken and cook for 10 minutes. Skim off fat from water.
Add vegetables, potatoes, tomato sauce and seasonings.
Cook on medium for 30 minutes.
Serve with your favorite noodles/pasta.

title: Spinach & Bacon Soup
fact: I acquired a great little specialty cookbook, Fessin’ Up by Sue Fess and had to add my favorite soup. I make this soup for my mom when she comes to visit me in San Antonio.
ingredients: 1 (10-ounce) package frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Sauté the onion, bacon, and garlic in a skillet until lightly browned. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Slowly add the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the onion and bacon mixture together with the spinach. Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Pour in heavy cream and white wine. Heat thoroughly, and season to taste with salt and pepper.

title: Grill Cheese Sandwich
fact: This quick and easy sandwich has been a quick snack for my sons and their friends throughout the years.
steps: Butter one side of two slices bread and place on pan.
Toast both sides of bread on skillet and place cheese between unbuttered side of toast, making a sandwich.
Grill both sides of sandwich until cheese is melted inside.
notes: Add a slice of ham when cooking bread and place on cheese to make a hot ham and cheese sandwich.

title: Tuna Salad
fact: Everyone has their own version of tuna salad. I love the original recipe I had growing up. Simple and satisfying.
ingredients: Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Add all ingredients into a bowl and mix.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve on butter lettuce for wraps or your favorite bread for sandwiches.

title: Italian Wedding Soup
fact: In the mid 90’s our family occasionally ate lunch on Sundays after mass at Spaghetti Warehouse. Years later I found their Italian Wedding Soup recipe in a magazine and make it on request — usually from Blake.
ingredients: 1 pound chicken breast meat, cooked and diced
1 cup cooked vermicelli, broken into quarters
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large stock pot.
Add chicken base. Stir to dissolve. Add celery, carrots, onion, spinach, and basil. Simmer 10 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and basil. Cook chicken (I use chicken tenders) in air fryer or oven for 15 minutes.
Meatballs: Place ground chuck in a large mixing bowl. Add breadcrumbs & cheese; set aside.
In blender, add onion, garlic, salt, pepper & eggs, and blend until chopped and mixed. Pour over ground chuck.
Mix by hand and shape into meatballs. Brown in skillet or air fryer on medium-low heat, drain.
Add cooked meatballs and chicken to the soup and cook on medium-low for 30 minutes.
Cook vermicelli and set aside to serve with soup.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
steps: Combine all ingredients in a slow cooker except chips and cheese.
Cook on high for 8 hours. Refrigerate overnight.
To serve, put a handful of chips in each bowl, ladle soup on top and sprinkle with cheese.
notes: If cooking on stovetop, cook on low heat, stirring frequently for 3 hours.

title: Shredded Lettuce Salad
fact: Alisson Del Papa made this salad for the Gary Thanksgiving in 2018 and has been the perfect go-to salad for lunch or dinner.
steps: Slice romaine heart lettuce very thin; slice and cut tomatoes into small pieces. Cut avocado into small pieces.
Slice purple onion very thin and cut into small pieces. Seed jalapeño and cut into very small pieces.
Finely chop cilantro.
Toss together and dress with fresh lemon or lime juice, salt, pepper, and a small amount of olive oil.

title: Chicken Gumbo
fact: This recipe was always a popular dish at Grace’s restaurant in Beaumont.
steps: Brown chicken in margarine; season with salt, pepper & Tony’s seasoning.
In a blender, blend celery, green onion & bell pepper and add to chicken while browning in skillet.
In a 10-quart pot add water and bring to a boil. Spoon in roux and stir until dissolved, stirring constantly so it does not stick.
Add chicken cooked in spices and cook on medium heat.
Slice and brown sausage in microwave. Drain grease and add to gumbo.
Cook on medium heat stirring occasionally for 1 hour. Serve with rice.

title: Italian Pasta Salad
fact: In the late 70’s at one of the many Marino family gatherings, I sampled this salad made by a classmate. I have been making it ever since. Great side for work potluck, special occasions and weekend family get-togethers.
steps: Boil vermicelli for 4 minutes and drain. Mix oil, steak seasoning, lemon juice and Tabasco.
Pour over hot vermicelli & chill for 3 hours.
Mix pimentos, black olives and sliced green onions and add to vermicelli once cooled.

title: Marinated Carrot Salad
fact: This recipe is another traditional side dish served at the Gary Thanksgiving and Christmas gatherings.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon each salt, black pepper, mustard, and Tabasco
steps: Pour water into a 3-quart pot and bring to a boil.
Add sliced carrots and cook until tender on low for 15 minutes.
In a separate bowl, mix together tomato soup, vinegar, salt, pepper, mustard, Tabasco, Worcestershire sauce, and sugar. Set aside.
Drain carrots and pour into a large bowl. Let cool completely. Top with onion and bell pepper.
Pour tomato soup mixture over carrots and marinate in refrigerator for 3 hours or overnight.

title: Crab Mousse
fact: This recipe is a traditional appetizer served at the Gary Thanksgiving and Christmas family gatherings. One of my mom’s favorite go-to dishes she makes for her bridge games at the Beaumont Bridge Studio.
ingredients: ½ cups green onion, fine chopped
steps: Bring water to a boil in a double boiler. Add soup and cheese and stir until smooth.
Reduce heat to low and add remaining ingredients to cheese mixture and mix.
Pour into Jell-O mold; chill until firm.

title: Carl’s Salsa
fact: February 2021, we had a taste test of 5 salsas from various local Mexican restaurants and homemade. Carl’s salsa placed 2nd with Henry’s Puffy Taco’s taking first place. Los Barrios salsa was the kids’ pick. I enjoy Carl’s salsa and prefer it anytime over the local Mexican restaurants.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a 5-quart pot.
Rinse tomatoes, peppers & cilantro. Cut off stems of peppers and tomatoes; set aside.
Cut stems off cilantro and put leafy part in blender. Cut onion into quarters and add ¾ in blender.
Once water comes to a boil add tomatoes and peppers and boil for 30 minutes.
Drain water from tomatoes and peppers and add to blender. Add salt and pepper and blend to desired consistency.
Serve with your favorite tortilla chips.

title: Bob Armstrong Dip
from: Matt’s El Rancho Restaurant, Austin TX
fact: One of our favorite Mexican restaurants in Austin is Matt’s El Rancho.
ingredients: ¼ cups red bell pepper, finely diced
Guacamole: 2 ripe avocados, peeled, pits removed
¼ cups red bell pepper, finely diced
¼ cups white onion, finely diced
2 cups shredded or cubed American cheese
steps: Meat: Heat a pot over medium heat, then add all meat ingredients. Cook, stirring, until the onion is translucent and meat is cooked, about 5 minutes. Keep warm.
Guacamole: Combine the avocados, lemon, granulated garlic, and oil, mashing everything slightly — chunky, not smooth. Stir in the tomato and season with salt.
Queso: Bring ¾ cup water to a boil in a small saucepan. Add the celery, bell pepper, onion, poblano and tomato and boil briefly about 1 minute.
Turn heat to low and gradually whisk in cheese. Heat a few minutes, stirring constantly. If too thick, add 1 tablespoon water until desired consistency. Remove from heat when melted.
Pour queso into a wide, shallow serving bowl. Add a scoop of meat and a scoop of guacamole. Do not mix — guests combine with tortilla chips as they eat.

title: Chicken Fricassee
fact: Enjoyed this dish at Emiel & Lena’s house in the late 1960’s. Usually served with black-eyed peas. I often made this dish for my kids growing up and now their children enjoy it.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. In a 13×9 or 10×10 baking dish coat bottom with margarine.
Pour rice and spread evenly. Layer chicken pieces on top of rice and pour soup over evenly.
Pour water over chicken and rice and place sliced bell pepper evenly. Add Texjoy seasoning and cook for 1 hour and 30 minutes.

title: Chili
fact: This is one of the first meals I cooked when Carl & I were married in 1974. We both worked and it was simple and quick. I still cook it the same way today.
ingredients: 1 can Ranch Style Beans with jalapeño peppers
steps: Brown ground chuck and beef sausage in a 5-quart pot. Drain excess grease.
Add Ranch Style Beans, McCormick’s seasoning mix, tomato sauce, water and stir.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 45 minutes stirring occasionally.
Serve with rice.

title: Cheese Lasagna
fact: Lasagna is one of my favorite Italian meals occasionally enjoyed at Lena & Emiel’s house since the late 60’s through the late 90’s. I still enjoy making this dish for my family on special occasions.
ingredients: 1 (48-ounce) jar of your favorite spaghetti sauce or homemade sauce
2 teaspoons parsley, dried or finely chopped
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 13×9-inch baking pan.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, eggs, Parmesan cheese, parsley and one cup of mozzarella cheese. Mix until well combined.
Place 1½ cups of spaghetti sauce in the bottom of the prepared baking pan. Gently place four lasagna noodles onto sauce.

Add about ⅓ of the cheese mixture to the top of the noodles, and gently spread across noodles. Top cheese with 1 cup of sauce, then noodles. Repeat one more time, finishing with a final layer of sauce.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake for 45 minutes. Remove foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes. Remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes prior to serving.
notes: Ground meat sauce may be substituted for ricotta cheese for a delicious meat lasagna.

title: Spaghetti & Meatballs
fact: I was first introduced to this wonderful dish in the late 70’s at the Marino’s. I had never tasted the flavor of a tomato spaghetti sauce like this before and still do not feel I have captured Lena’s sauce, but it is close. Lena served this dish most Sundays as her mother (Carmela) did — an Italian family tradition.
steps: Sauce: In a 2½-quart pot sauté onion & garlic in oil for 15 minutes. Add tomato paste and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes stirring occasionally.
While paste is simmering, in a 10-quart pot add water, sugar, salt and heat on high.
Pour cooked tomato paste into sugar water and reduce heat to medium-low. Cook at least 2 hours prior to adding meatballs, stirring occasionally.
Meatballs: Place ground chuck in a large mixing bowl. Add breadcrumbs & cheese; set aside.
In blender, add onion, garlic, salt, pepper & eggs, and blend until chopped and mixed. Pour over ground chuck.
Mix by hand and shape into meatballs. Brown in skillet or air fryer on medium-low heat, drain and add to sauce. Cover and cook on low heat for 2 to 8 hours.
notes: The longer the sauce cooks, the better the flavor. I usually start cooking the sauce 2 days prior to serving, leaving on low overnight. I add the meatballs the following day and let them cook all day and overnight, serving the next day. Serve with spaghetti & garlic bread.

title: Squash Casserole
fact: This recipe is another traditional side dish served at the Gary Thanksgiving and Christmas gatherings.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cook squash on medium heat in a 2½-quart pot for 15 minutes. Pour into a 9×13-inch baking dish. Sauté onion & celery in margarine. Stir in soup and sour cream; pour over cooked squash.
Top with breadcrumbs and cheese and bake for 20 to 30 minutes.

title: Cornbread Dressing
fact: This recipe is another traditional side dish served at the Gary Thanksgiving and Christmas gatherings.
ingredients: 1 pound spicy sausage (Owens or Jimmy Dean)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Cook cornbread according to directions. Cool and crumble; set aside.
Brown sausage, drain and set aside.
Sauté onion, bell pepper & celery in oil for 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Wet cornbread with melted butter and chicken broth. Add remaining ingredients and mix.
Put in buttered casserole dish, cover, and cook for 30 minutes.

title: Sausage & Potatoes
fact: This dish was one of Lena’s go-to quick meals that always was a family favorite. The Marino’s bought their meat at the packing house and always had the best flavor.
ingredients: 5 medium russet potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 pound Zummo beef or Party Time sausage, sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Pour oil in skillet and add potatoes, browning on both sides.
Add sausage and continue to brown sausage with potatoes. Season with Texjoy, chili pepper, salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 20 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are cooked.

title: Stones Baked Beans
fact: In the mid-70’s a co-worker of Carl’s brought this dish to a potluck luncheon and I decided I had to keep the recipe as a side dish. Since that time, I have been making it for my family.
ingredients: Italian seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, and red and black pepper, to taste
steps: In a 2-quart pot add all ingredients, cover and cook on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
notes: Sauté onion & bacon prior to adding all ingredients (optional).

title: Taco & Rice
fact: This recipe was a weekly dish at Mee-maw and Pawpaw Marino’s house. Still served today at my house.
steps: Brown ground chuck in skillet; drain excess grease.
Add taco seasoning mix and water according to package. Add Ranch Style Beans, cover and cook on medium-low for 20 minutes.
Put water in 2½-quart pot and bring to a boil. Add rice and let water boil down to just above the rice. Cover and reduce heat to low and cook for 20 minutes.

title: Pizza
fact: I started making homemade pizzas in the early 90’s using the Kraft mixes and yeast packet dough instructions for the crust from HEB. I later bought a bread cookbook “Bread in Half the Time,” occasionally using their recipe and my family’s favorite toppings.
ingredients: 1 jar of your favorite pizza sauce
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Combine warm water, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl. Let proof for 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, olive oil, salt and stir well with a wooden spoon or mix in a stand mixer with a dough hook until combined.
Knead for 5 minutes using stand mixer with a dough hook attachment or 6 minutes by hand until smooth and elastic.
Drizzle a clean bowl with a little olive oil, then place the ball of dough in the bowl and turn it to coat. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes or until double in size.
Roll, pat or stretch the dough out until it is ¼ inch thick. Place on round or square baking sheet. Top with sauce, cheese, and meat topping.
Bake 5 to 10 minutes until cheese is melted and crust is golden brown and crispy around the edges. Cool slightly before cutting and serving.

title: Brown Gravy & Rice
fact: This recipe was created from a dish Lena Marino served weekly made with the brown gravy mix. Lena cooked a roast with this mix in the oven. I revised it using a crockpot in place of the oven.
ingredients: 2 (4.5-ounce) packages brown gravy mix (Southeastern Mills Classic)
steps: Place chicken in the crockpot and turn on to Low.
Season with Texjoy steak seasoning and red pepper flakes.
In a 2½–3-quart pot make brown gravy according to package directions and pour over chicken.
Add bell pepper, cover, and cook on low for 6 hours stirring occasionally.
Serve over rice.
notes: Roast may be substituted for chicken. If using 1.76-ounce brown gravy mix packets, use 3 packages.

title: Italian Green Beans
fact: Lena Marino made green beans and potatoes often using regular cut green beans. I still make them today as she did but using Italian cut green beans and a small addition of red pepper flakes.
steps: Cut sliced potatoes in half and brown in olive oil in sauce pot.
Pour can of green beans over browned potatoes and season with Texjoy and red pepper flakes.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes.

title: Street Tacos
fact: Brian & Jessica sampled street tacos while in Reynosa, Mexico in 2012. Since that time he makes his own street tacos at home usually once or twice a month for family and friends.
ingredients: 1 package (20 to 50 count) Guerrero mini corn tortillas
steps: Place beef skirt steak on the grill, season with Fiesta Beef Fajita Seasoning and grill for 8–12 minutes on each side depending on thickness.
Remove steaks and cut into small cubes. Place in skillet and add chopped red and orange mini peppers. Cook on medium/low for about 5 to 10 minutes.
Place corn tortillas on grill and cook for 2–4 minutes on each side.
Assemble taco and garnish with avocado, green onion, lime juice, El Yucateco salsa and shredded cheese.
notes: Ground beef may be substituted for skirt steak. Photo by Jessica Marino.

title: Chicken Pasta Toss
fact: Denise won this recipe and wooden bread basket at a St. Agnes Academy faculty luncheon in Houston. The Stasio’s have enjoyed this dinner for many years and have served it often to friends & family.
ingredients: 2 cooked chicken breasts, cut into strips
steps: Cook pasta until almost done — pasta should still be chewy. Add broccoli into pot with pasta and cook for 3 minutes.
Strain pasta and broccoli. Pour pasta into a large serving bowl, add cooked chicken, sundried tomatoes, Parmesan cheese and toss.
Serve with bread sticks and salad of your choice.

title: Barbeque Ribs
fact: Grampa Joe O’Bryant came up with his own special barbeque sauce in the early 70’s during one of their many family barbeques — still made today and Dusty’s favorite dish.
ingredients: Sauce: 2 (18-ounce) bottles Original Kraft BBQ sauce
2 (18-ounce) bottles Hickory Smoke Kraft BBQ sauce
Meat: baby back ribs, as needed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Sauce: Pour all ingredients into a pot and stir until mixed.
Bring mixture to a boil stirring constantly for about a minute. Reduce heat to low and cook for 4–5 hours.
Meat: Lightly salt and pepper both sides of ribs.
Grill ribs on a gas grill for about 1½ hours, turning often.
Transfer to charcoal grill applying the sauce to both sides as you turn the ribs.
The longer you baste the ribs and the slower you cook, the better the taste.

title: Biscotti
fact: These cookies are a Christmas tradition. I usually made these for my Bunco group and work holiday parties. Always a big hit.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl mix flour, baking powder, salt, anise seeds and nuts together. Cut in Crisco and butter. Set aside.
In a medium bowl mix sugar, eggs, vanilla, almond extract, and Anisette.
Pour egg mixture over flour mixture and mix well. Roll and form into logs about 8–10 inches long and 2 inches wide.
Bake 35 minutes or until brown at 350°F. Remove from oven, slice, and brush with Anisette.
Place sliced biscotti evenly on cookie sheet and bake at 400° until brown. Turn over, brush with Anisette and cook other side until brown. Let cool completely before storing.

title: Martha Washington’s
fact: In the mid 70’s at one of the many Marino gatherings with friends & family, I tasted this sweet treat. At that time called “Chocolate Dips” and later discovered the real name “Old fashion Martha Washington candy”. Since that time, I’ve made them for holidays, work potlucks and Bunco games.
ingredients: ¾ block household paraffin wax (Gulf wax)
steps: Mix together sugar, coconut, milk, butter, pecans & vanilla. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Roll into marble-size balls and place on wax paper. Chill in refrigerator while melting chocolate dipping sauce.
Melt in double boiler chocolate & wax. Dip ball in chocolate with toothpick & place on wax paper.

title: Cinnamon Streusel Cake
fact: I originally baked this cake for CarlMichael’s birthday celebrations throughout the years. Today I bake it for any occasion as a dessert for family gatherings. It has become a family favorite.
ingredients: Cake: 1 box yellow cake mix (Betty Crocker butter cake mix)
steps: Streusel: In a small bowl, stir together the streusel ingredients. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a 10 or 12-cup Bundt pan and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the cake and pudding mixes. Add milk and water and stir to combine. Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla. Beat for 6 minutes at high speed.
Pour half the batter into the prepared Bundt pan, sprinkle with all the streusel mixture, then pour remaining batter over the top. Bake for 55 minutes.
Cool cake for 8 minutes, then turn out of pan and let cool completely.
Glaze: Beat together all ingredients until smooth and drizzle over cooled cake.

title: Granny’s Angel Food Cake
fact: Growing up angel food cake was my favorite cake, usually topped with strawberries & whipped cream. Dusty & I share our love for this simple cake that we both enjoyed every year on our birthdays. This recipe is from Dusty’s Granny who also chose this cake for her birthday every year.
ingredients: Cake: 1 box angel food cake mix (Duncan Hines)
steps: Remove top oven rack; move remaining rack to lowest position. Preheat oven to 350°F. Do not grease the pan.
Blend cake mix and water in a large bowl at low speed until moistened (about 30 seconds). Beat at medium speed for 1 minute. Pour into ungreased 10-inch tube pan and bake immediately.
Bake for 38 to 48 minutes. Cake is done when top is golden brown and cracked, looks very dry and is firm to touch. Do not underbake.
Hang pan upside down on heat-proof glass bottle until completely cool, about 1½ hours. Loosen edges carefully with flat knife or spatula to remove cake.
Cut cake into 3 layers and add the whipped icing between layers, top & sides.
Icing: Beat together sugar & whipping cream until stiff peaks form. Do not overbeat or it will turn to butter.
notes: Favorite fresh fruit & whipped cream may be substituted for icing. Best to cut with an electric knife.

title: Tipsy Pudding
fact: This dessert was made by Julia and served at Momo’s (Grandmother Bordages) house growing up. This family recipe is still made by my mom every Thanksgiving & Christmas during the family gatherings.
ingredients: 2½ envelopes Knox gelatin, dissolve in cherry juice
12 almond macaroons, broken up (Italian bakery cookies from HEB)
steps: Cut cherries, pecans, cookies and line the bottom of the baking dish. Set aside.
Heat milk to warm. Beat egg yolks, add to sugar; when milk is warm add eggs and sugar stirring constantly.
Bring almost to a boil (about 10 minutes).
Mix gelatin with cherry juice. Beat egg whites and add to gelatin mixture. Add to milk mixture when it is room temperature.
Stir until very cool. Stir in whiskey. Pour over cookies, cherries, nuts. Put in refrigerator. Top with whipped cream when serving.

title: Original Toll House Cookies
fact: I started making these cookies in the early 60’s with my sisters. A family favorite. Simple and timeless.
ingredients: ¾ cups firmly packed brown sugar
1 (12-ounce) package (2 cups) Nestlé Toll House semi-sweet chocolate morsels
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. In a small bowl, combine flour, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine butter, sugar, brown sugar, and vanilla extract; beat until creamy. Beat in eggs. Gradually add flour mixture.
Stir in Nestlé Toll House semi-sweet chocolate morsels and nuts. Drop by level tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake for 9–11 minutes.
Pan cookie variation: Spread dough into greased 15½×10½×1-inch baking pan. Bake at 375°F for 20–25 minutes. Cool completely. Cut into thirty-five 2-inch squares.

title: Sugar Cookies
fact: Lillian shared this recipe with me after she started baking her own made-to-order cookies. This cookie recipe was used (with a slight variation) for Lucas & Paula’s wedding (Lillian’s brother – 11/11/22). This is my go-to sugar cookie recipe now. Always turns out delicious.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder and salt. Set aside.
In a stand mixer or with a hand mixer, cream together butter and sugar for about 2 minutes until light and fluffy. Add the eggs and mix until incorporated. Scrape down the sides.
Add vanilla, almond extract and cream cheese. Mix until combined. Scrape down the sides again.
Add dry ingredients in 2 to 3 batches. Mix on low until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
Turn dough out onto plastic wrap. Wrap tightly and refrigerate at least 4 hours (up to 2 weeks).
Roll dough out on a floured surface, ¼ inch thick. Preheat oven to 350°F and cut into desired shapes. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes.

title: Rosette Cookies
fact: A traditional cookie made at the Stasio’s house in New York during the Christmas season.
steps: Combine eggs, sugar & salt in a medium size mixing bowl and beat well.
Add flour, milk, vanilla and beat until smooth.
Heat rosette iron in 2 to 3 inches hot oil for a minute or so before placing for the first time into batter.
Dip hot rosette iron into batter ¾ the way up the iron for about 5 seconds. Carefully remove from batter and immediately fry until golden brown — about 30 seconds. Lift out and drain excess oil.
Place rosette onto paper towel on a wire rack. Reheat iron, drain & repeat.
Sift powdered sugar over cooled rosettes.

title: Pecan Pie
fact: A holiday favorite that my sisters and I made often growing up.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix sugar and eggs together. Add Karo, salt, vanilla extract and butter. Stir in pecans and pour into pie shell. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Banana Pudding
fact: Lena’s banana pudding was always a treat for her family. The boys loved to eat the pudding hot as she finished mixing it in the serving bowl.
ingredients: 1 can water (equal to evaporated milk can)
steps: Add milk and water in a pot and warm on medium. Add butter and stir until blended.
In a separate bowl mix sugar and flour together and gradually add to milk and stir until blended.
Add beaten eggs to milk and flour mixture in pot and bring to a boil. Add vanilla extract after pudding thickens.
In a serving bowl, alternate vanilla wafers, bananas, and pudding.

title: Miami Vice
fact: I first enjoyed this drink on a Caribbean cruise we went on with Carl & Dusty in the summer of 2019. In December of 2020 we went to Hawaii for Christmas with the family and this drink was known as a Lava Flow.
ingredients: 16 ounces Piña Colada mix (Master of Mixers)
16 ounces strawberry daiquiri mix (Master of Mixers)
steps: Add ice in the blender.
Pour 5 ounces Malibu over ice.
Add Piña Colada mix and blend for 30 seconds. Pour mixing glasses half full and set aside.
Prepare daiquiri drink using steps 1–3 with strawberry daiquiri mix in place of piña colada mix.
Pour strawberry daiquiri drink over piña colada drink in half-filled glasses.
Garnish with pineapple wedge.

title: Hawaiian Mai Tai
fact: My favorite signature drink from the bar at Lillian & Blake’s awesome & breathtaking wedding in Hawaii (2/11/23).
steps: Combine rum, Grand Marnier, orgeat syrup, and lime juice.
Shake or stir with ice and serve.
Garnish as desired.
notes: Amounts as preferred — signature wedding bar pour.

title: Frozen Margarita
fact: My favorite frozen margaritas are made at Los Barrios Restaurant here in San Antonio. When making them at home, Cheri Marino uses this recipe most like Los Barrios frozen margaritas.
steps: Add ice to blender.
Pour frozen lime juice over ice in blender. Add 6 ounces tequila and blend for 30 seconds or desired consistency.
Pour into drinking glasses and top with 1 ounce Grand Marnier.
Garnish with lime slice.
